desc:
The numbers of top are written in order along an upper row and the numbers of bottom in order along a lower row. You may draw straight line segments, each joining one number of the upper row to an equal number of the lower row.

No number may be an endpoint of more than one segment, and no two segments may cross each other (segments that would meet at a shared endpoint are not allowed anyway). Return the maximum number of segments you can draw.

top = [1, 4, 2], bottom = [1, 2, 4]  ->  2   (join 1-1 and either 4-4 or 2-2, not both)
top = [2, 5, 1, 2, 5], bottom = [10, 5, 2, 1, 5, 2]  ->  3
hints: Two segments (i1, j1) and (i2, j2) do not cross exactly when i1 < i2 and j1 < j2, or the reverse. What kind of structure is a set of pairwise non-crossing segments?
Read the chosen pairs from left to right: the upper indices increase, the lower indices increase, and the values are equal. So the values form a sequence that is a subsequence of both arrays.
The task is the longest common subsequence of the two arrays. Use dp[i][j] for the first i and first j numbers, extending diagonally on equal values and otherwise taking the larger neighbour.
editorial: A segment joins position i of the top row to position j of the bottom row, and two segments avoid crossing exactly when their endpoints are ordered the same way on both rows. Sorting the segments by their upper endpoint therefore also sorts them by their lower endpoint. The values along the segments form a sequence that appears, in order, in both arrays, i.e. a common subsequence. Conversely, any common subsequence gives a valid set of non-crossing segments by matching the chosen positions in order.

So the answer is the length of the longest common subsequence. Let dp[i][j] be that length for the prefixes of sizes i and j. If top[i-1] == bottom[j-1] we can add a segment between them: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1. Otherwise one of the two numbers is unused: dp[i][j] = max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]). Only the previous row is needed, giving O(n) memory.
